newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria deputy PM heads bank consolidation firm.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria deputy PM heads bank consolidation firm.

text.p: Bulgaria's deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev was appointed on Tuesday to head the Bank Consolidation Company (BCC), set up four years ago to merge and privatise some of the country's numerous and illiquid banks.

The previous chairman of the BCC board, Dimitar Dimitrov, announced the appointment to reporters after a board meeting. Dimitrov, who is also deputy central bank governor, becomes deputy board chairman.
Gechev has cabinet responsibility for economic policy.

The BCC, which manages state equity in nine commercial banks, was expected to conclude its operations by February. "But BCC's functioning can be extended until it completes its bank privatisation tasks," said Gechev.

BCC's short-term goals include selling off some of the 14 banks which the central bank placed under special supervision earlier this year with the aim of seeking their insolvency through the courts, said Gechev. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, +359-2-84561
